text:
England dispatched Costa Rica 3-0 in their final World Cup warm-up match in Orlando. They were slow to start after a thunderstorm delayed kick-off by an hour, but soon found themselves in the ascendancy against their opponents.

Declan Rice opened the scoring after good work from Anthony Gordon in the first half, as the Three Lions struggled to capitalise on their ascendancy.

It was Gordon who stepped up to double England's lead from the spot in the second period, with Harry Kane off the field. Eberechi Eze's strike found an elbow and the Barcelona star fired in an unstoppable penalty.

Ollie Watkins showed exactly why he was on the plane by tapping in after Aston Villa team-mate Morgan Rogers had his shot from distance saved. The goal capped off a dominant outing that still tested Tuchel's side in a few areas.

The German coach also had a boost in Bukayo Saka coming off the bench after Tuchel had highlighted an injury concern for the Arsenal star. He will have a further opportunity to prove his readiness in a behind-closed-doors friendly on Thursday.

Follow all the latest with Mirror Football here.

England's last friendly was a positive step forward, and they will have another to make in their behind-closed-doors friendly tomorrow, against Miami FC. Thomas Tuchel knows his team for that game tomorrow, and it will be full of players who played fewer minutes this evening.

After that, it's Croatia and the World Cup. It's finally here.

Oh, Mexico vs South Africa is in less than 20 hours too. Strap yourselves in.

Bellingham might have done enough to give Tuchel confidence in his position. Gordon certainly put in a decent audition too. Gordon or Rashford remains a tough one.

Keane believes that's a good thing.

Tuchel is not in a rush.

Thomas Tuchel is pleased with the team spirit and what England showed this evening.

Roy Keane reckons the German coach will be pleased, and we know about the ex-Manchester United's standards when it comes to World Cup preparations...

Not perfect, but a three-goal win and another step towards the tournament. Things looked more lively after the subs but Costa Rica were probably tired.

The journey begins now.

Stoppage time remains in Orlando but we've ticked past midnight which means the World Cup starts later today!

Here we go!

The fans are singing that song as they feel just a little bit better about the team's chances after three goals.

Could it be?

Watkins finds the net this time. The Aston Villa forward poaches a goal after Rogers' strike was saved by the goalkeeper.

The England winger is getting plenty of cheers as he walks across to take a corner. Definitely appears to be a popular figure.

Tuchel's men still putting on pressure but not creating too much of note. Costa Rica clean up as Watkins tries to sniff a chance.

We're nearly 80n minutes into the match but things are opening up for England now and they're generating some chances.

Rogers had a disappointing finish a few minutes ago but Mainoo and Eze are looking lively and are inspiring some atmosphere in Orlando.

Rashford, Maino, Quansah, Watkins and Burn have entered the field. Shortlived time up front for Bellingham.

Strong effort from 12 yards and Gordon doubles England's lead.

Eze hits the ball and it's blocked by an elbow. It's getting checked.

This one remains, Gordon to take.

Sequira does now go off to be replaced my Madriz.

England get going too.

Eze on for Rice.

Spence on for James.

Saka on for Madueke.

Guehi on for Stones.

Henderson on for Pickford.

Rogers on for Kane.

No striker on the pitch, looks like Bellingham is moving upfield.

Sequeira was down for a long time on the field and seems to be continuing after his treatment. Fans aren't impressed and Tuchel isn't either.

England have recorded 81 per cent possession so far.

12 shots and four on target so far. Costa Rica have had just one shot. Few more goals wouldn't go amiss.

The supporters aren't happy as Costa Rica's goalkeeper, Patrick Sequeira, goes down to receive treatment. He is going to be replaced.

It's into the low 30s pitchside and the humidity is still over 70 per cent. Definitely a bit toasty for England and that's probably good for the players to get used to.

Thomas Tuchel watches on(Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

This isn't just for the England team but for everyone at home too. It's going to be tough transitioning to these late games for the next month or so but we can do it.

Everyone remember your fluids. We can sleep during pre-season.

England have Costa Rica penned in for the moment.

We're underway for England's final 45 minutes before the World Cup.

The sun looks like it's beaming by the way.

The teams have taken to the pitch, and the changes are coming later.

Let's see what they can do in the next 15 minutes.

The players might be safe to stay on the pitch until after the break. It sounded like Tuchel suggested Harry Kane would play 60 minutes, so perhaps that is when the subs will come.

Harry Kane against Costa Rica(Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Roy Keane just wants to see end product from Anthony Gordon and Noni Madueke. Speaking on ITV he said the full-back 'looked frightened to death'.

Our man in Orlando, John Cross, has given his verdict on the opening half. Bellingham has been the man for him and there's not been much to mark down.

England (4-2-3-1)

Jordan Pickford 6

Made himself busy after shanking one clearance which presented Costa Rica with a rare chance.

Reece James 7

You can see why he is first choice right back. Tenacious, strong and good going forward.

John Stones 7

Looks classy on the pitch. Elegant, strong and largely untroubled. Good audition.

Ezri Konsa 7

Quick and dependable. He was often the last man and just ran the game in front of him.

Nico O’Reilly 7

Often pushed up into midfield to make things happen. Easy to see why he should start against Croatia.

Declan Rice 8

Carried on where he left off for Arsenal. Driving runs, opening goal and great free kicks.

Elliot Anderson 7

All the talk of a £100m-plus move to Manchester City has not put him off his game.

Jude Bellingham 9

Got the nod ahead of Morgan Rogers - and showed why. He looked so fired up.

Noni Madueke 7

A first half miss will go down as one of the all-time great England bloopers. Missed an open goal.

Anthony Gordon 8

Was so dangerous. Looked quick, razor sharp and a real threat. This was him laying down a marker to start ahead of Rashford.

Harry Kane 7

England’s Captain Marvel is dropping too deep. He’s a class apart but he needs to stay forward.

Jude Bellingham made his claim(Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

An improvement from against New Zealand or just weaker opponents?

A solid run out nevertheless.

Lee Dixon doesn't think it's a penalty and the referee agrees. Decision overturned.

He did go down very easily but it looked clumsy from the defender.
